Laura / Alex —

Thanks again for the call today. Per our discussion I sketched an initial mutual action plan (attached) that captures the evaluation checkpoints we agreed on and three hosting options we should validate in week 1 of the MAP: Hosted (fastest to production), Dedicated (reserved capacity, better P95 guarantees), Private/VPC (on-prem or customer-managed).

High level asks from Nexa: privacy controls, regional deployment in EU due to data residency, predictable latency for clinical inference (P95 < 120ms), and SSO/KMS integration.

Proposed short MAP:
- Week 0 (today–Aug 7): confirm deployment mode candidates and any non-negotiable compliance items; vendor to provide SOC2 checklist and regional latency numbers.
- Week 1 (Aug 8–14): run a 2-day hosted pilot in eu-west-1 (smoke), a dedicated capacity estimate, and security questionnaire baseline.
- Week 2 (Aug 15–21): perf validation and SLA pricing for Dedicated; if Dedicated required, draft procurement term sheet and PO timeline.

Attachments: NexaHealth_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP milestones + owners), security_evidence_checklist.pdf (SOC2 checklist + evidences we can provide).

Key decisions we need from you this week:
1) Confirm that EU region (eu-west-1) is acceptable for the pilot and preferred for production.
2) Indicate any absolute requirements that eliminate Hosted or Dedicated (e.g., air-gapped on-prem).
3) Procurement lead + timing so we can align pricing/commitment options.

I'll loop in Priyom and Rishi for technical/runbook details. Happy to run a short walkthrough of the MAP tomorrow.

Best,

Laura / team — quick follow on technical fit for the commitment options.

1) Hosted: fastest onboarding (API keys, ephemeral accounts). We can deploy a smoke test in eu-west-1 within 48 hours. Hosted supports CMEK for dedicated customers via key-in-transit to our KMS integrations; full customer-managed HSM is available for Private.

2) Dedicated: reserved GPU pool pinned to eu-west-1. Provides predictable P95 latency and can be configured with dedicated KV cache. Typical procurement lead for Dedicated baseline commitment (8–16 GPUs equivalent) is 3–4 weeks after PO depending on capacity alignment.

3) Private/VPC: available but requires a longer setup window (4–8 weeks), network review, and an on-site or VPC peering checklist. This typically converts to an enterprise license and support contract.

For the MAP pilot I propose: run Hosted smoke in eu-west-1 (2 days) to validate inference correctness and latency, simultaneously produce a Dedicated capacity estimate and pricing. That lets Nexa prove the feature quickly while giving procurement numbers for Dedicated.

I'll attach a short-runbook (inline below) and can run the pilot with your ops lead.

Runbook (high level):
- Day 1: small dataset sample (500 requests) through hosted eu-west-1 endpoint, capture P50/P95/P99 and token cost.
- Day 2: stress run with parallel clients (up to expected QPS) to surface latency tail behavior.
- End of Day 2: deliver results and recommended hosting mode.

If procurement needs earlier price points I can provide a quick ballpark by Aug 7.

—Priyom
Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference

Adding engineering confidence numbers — we ran a short bench in eu-west-1 last month on the model family you mentioned. Expected numbers for Nexa's median payload:
- Hosted (shared pool): P50 ~ 34ms, P95 ~ 110ms, P99 ~ 190ms under light tail; with continuous batching P95 improves ~10–15%.
- Dedicated (8 GPU equiv pool): P50 ~ 30ms, P95 ~ 75–95ms, very stable tail under sustained load.

Notes: cold-start behavior is more visible in Hosted when requests are sparse; Dedicated reduces that variance. For compliance items — SOC2 Type II and CMEK for encryption at rest with customer-managed keys are both supported. Private deployment supports HSM-based keys if that's required.

I'll help instrument the pilot to capture P95 with the same payload and a 99th percentile guardrails so procurement can see the delta.

Rishi
Senior Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
